Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:34: Proof of this, from the passage concerning that wicked man, who said (Genesis 34:19) "and the young man did not delay to do the thing, because he desired Jacob's daughter" - and the desire for her was because she was the daughter of a great man, our father Jacob, peace be upon him; for a person should not delay performing and completing a mitzvah even though he knows harm may come to him from it, like that wicked man - for even though the matter touched his body and soul in the matter of circumcision, which is nearly dangerous, he did not delay doing it because of his desire for Jacob's daughter, as we explained - so one should not delay performing a mitzvah because of his yearning and desire for it. For every single mitzvah is "the daughter of Jacob," as is known, comprising two hundred and forty-eight mitzvot, and every mitzvah is comprised of two hundred and forty-eight, as I explained above; we find, then, that every mitzvah is a complete stature.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:35: When he considers the reality of the mitzvah, in the One who commands it, and the speed of performing the mitzvah, and that he does not delay in performing it, this indicates his abundant yearning for it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:36: Therefore he must free himself from all worldly occupations and all his thoughts, so that the will of his soul be strengthened within him and his soul cleave and be enflamed in performing it, to such a degree that even if all the money in the world were given him, he would not stop performing it - just as a person would not delay uniting with his wife when his ultimate yearning is for her, even were he given all the money in the world - so his ultimate yearning should be for the mitzvah, since through performing it he unites with the King's daughter, who is the Shechinah, daughter of Jacob - every woman is "the daughter of her husband," as is said of Mordechai (Esther 2:7) "Mordechai took her as his daughter" [alluding to a secret union] - and it is not fitting to delay the union, but rather to strive with speed and great alacrity in performing the mitzvah, and through this he cleaves to the supernal life and his soul shines with the illumination of the supernal light shining in the performance of that mitzvah. We shall further elaborate below, with the Lord's help, on hints to the greatness of the mitzvot.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:37: Because of the reason mentioned, you will find that it does not say "his soul desired [chafetzah] Jacob's daughter," as it says above (Genesis 34:8) "for Shechem my son, his soul yearns," and likewise "his soul cleaved" - because here [in the final verse] he was giving over his soul and body, therefore it says simply "desired," comprising all.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:38: In cleaving to this great yearning, a person must have yearning for the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, and this is the matter of "and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your might" (Deuteronomy 6:5); Rashbi, of blessed memory, explains that "and you shall love the Lord your God" is said concerning the love of the Shechinah - his words (Zohar, Terumah 155b): he opened and said, (Psalms 119:126) "it is time to act for the Lord, they have made void Your Torah" - "it is time to act for the Lord" - there is a time and there is a time, (Ecclesiastes 3:8) "a time to love and a time to hate" - "time" is above, for that "time" is the secret of faith [Malchut], and this is called "an acceptable time," and it is this for which a person is obligated to love the Lord always, as it says "and you shall love the Lord your God"; therefore "a time to love" is the time a person is obligated to love, and there is another "time," which is the secret of "other gods," and a person is obligated to hate it and not let his heart be drawn after it - and this is "a time to hate" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:39: This is likewise explained further in Ra'aya Meheimna (Terumah 158b), where Rashbi, peace be upon him, praises Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, saying: "you fulfilled, concerning the Shechinah, 'and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart,' meaning the body; 'and with all your soul,' meaning the neshamah, which has five names - Neshamah, Ruach, Nefesh, Chayah, Yechidah; 'and with all your might' - with all your money. The Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah will not depart from you through all these. You considered that even were all the worlds under your dominion, you would have given them to raise up the Shechinah with the Holy One, blessed be He, and to proclaim His sovereignty with His Shechinah over all the appointees of the nations of the world, and afterward to raise Him and His Shechinah in your own image, comprised of all good attributes, in all the worlds and among the supernal and lower camps and over all Israel. A good thought, the Holy One, blessed be He, joins to the deed - after you were created, whatever you thought for your Master, He fulfills through you, and He will never move from you, but you shall be in His image in everything" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:40: Further, in the Tikkunim (37a) - their words: "the gift given to the Shechinah must be made from that which is most dear to him, as the masters of the Mishnah established: 'and you shall love the Lord' with that which is dear to you" - so far, their words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:41: Our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (Berachot 61b): there is a person whose body is dearer to him than his money, therefore it says "with all your soul" [i.e., even if it costs your life]; and vice versa, "with all your might" - a person should hold the Holy One, blessed be He, dear with whatever is dearest to him. And they explain this passage in the Tikkunim (141a) - their words: there is fear and there is love: there is one who fears the Holy One, blessed be He, so that his children be granted grace or that he not descend into poverty, or loves Him because He gives him wealth and tests him, [saying] "now let us do this and see whether the Lord is among us and gives us reward for it"; if not - for if He does not give him reward for it, he does not love Him, does not give charity, and does not perform a mitzvah - and he certainly tests the Holy One, blessed be He; this is among that evil mixture of which it is said (Exodus 17:7) "is the Lord among us, or not?" Rather, love and fear of the Holy One, blessed be He, is complete whether He gives him reward with goodness or does not give it to him. Therefore the Torah commands (Deuteronomy 6:5) "and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your might," and the earlier sages established: if your soul is dearer to you than your money, therefore it says "with all your soul"; and if your money is dearer to you than your soul, therefore it says "with all your might" - a person who performs all the commandments and prays without receiving reward for them - and had he received reward for them, would he not have performed them? For certainly there are many people who are exceedingly wealthy, and they hold their wealth dearer than their own soul, since the wealth of the soul consists of good deeds in the World to Come, while the wealth of the body is money and the pleasures of this world; and those who hold money dearer than soul - even were they given the whole Torah for a hundred zuz, they would not give it up for it, since money is dearer to them than the soul, and whoever fears and loves Him only for the sake of money, making money the essence and the Torah he loves secondary, this love and fear the Holy One, blessed be He, does not value.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:42: Rather, the essence of love and fear of the Holy One, blessed be He, is that although he loves his money more than his soul, he loves Him with his money in the part he considers primary, not in what is secondary to him - therefore it says "and with all your might." And likewise he should hold his soul dearer than his money, and give up all the money in the world rather than be harmed even in a small limb - therefore it says "with all your soul," with what is dear to him - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:43: Just as desire is found in the matter of performing the mitzvot, so it should be found in engaging in the study of Torah - that the will of the soul strengthen within him and all the senses of the body be nullified, and his soul cleave in the contemplation of the Torah until he feels nothing of the matters of this world, as our Sages, of blessed memory, say in the Talmud (Shabbat 88a) concerning Rava, who was studying with his hand beneath him, and blood was flowing from his fingernails, and he did not feel the blood coming from him, due to his great cleaving to the Torah. And I have likewise heard from many of the later sages that they had this great cleaving to the Torah, such that they felt nothing of the matters of this world at all. For just as one who is enamored of his beloved nullifies all his other thoughts, and the fire of love for her burns in his heart, such that whether he eats or drinks or sleeps, all his thoughts are of his beloved, so a person should have love of the Creator, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:44: This is likewise learned from a story Rabbi Yitzchak of Acre, of blessed memory, writes: one day the king's daughter went out from the bathhouse, and a certain idle man saw her, and he sighed a great sigh and said, "would that she were in my power, to do with her as I see fit." The king's daughter answered him and said, "in the house of graves this shall be, and not here." Hearing these words, he rejoiced, thinking she meant for him to go to the house of graves and sit there, and she would come to him and he would do with her as he saw fit. But she did not intend this; rather, she meant to say that specifically there, small and great are equal, young and old, lowly and honored - (Job 3:19) "small and great are there" - there all become equal, but here, not so, for it is not fitting that any of the common people approach the king's daughter.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:45: That man arose and went to the house of graves, and sat there, and bound the thought of his mind to her, always thinking of her form, and out of his great yearning for her, he stripped his thought of everything sensory and placed it all in the form of that woman and her beauty; day and night he sat continually in the house of graves, and there he ate and drank and slept, for he said, "if she does not come today, she will come tomorrow" - so he did for many days.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:46: Out of his great abstinence from everything sensory, in binding his mind's thought to one thing continually, and his solitude and complete yearning, his soul was stripped of sensory things and returned to cleave to intelligibles, until it was stripped of everything sensory, even of the woman, and cleaved to the Name, blessed be He, so that within a few days he had stripped away everything sensory, and his yearning was for the divine intelligible, and he became a complete servant, a man of God, holy, until his prayer was heard and his blessing worked for all the travelers who passed by that way, and merchants and horsemen and pedestrians who passed that way would turn aside to him and receive his blessing, until his name spread far and wide - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:47: He further elaborates there on the merit of this ascetic, and Rabbi Yitzchak of Acre, peace be upon him, writes there, in the stories of the ascetics, that whoever has not yearned for a woman is like a donkey and lower than it - the reason being that from the sensory one must discern divine service, as we have explained, and with this the exact meaning of the word "chefetz" [desire] is understood.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 4:48: From this story we learn that whoever yearns for Torah so greatly that day and night he thinks of nothing in the world but it, will certainly attain a wondrous level in his soul, and need no mortifications or fasts, for cleaving depends only on yearning and love of Torah, to the point that he yearns for it as he would love his beloved, along with the constancy of rising at midnight with yearning, as is explained in its place, with the Lord's help.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:1: This chapter concerns the matters that give birth to love, and I have chosen to quote here what the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot writes on this matter (Gate of the Love of God, chapter 3) - his words: the author says, but what is the path to the love of God, blessed be He? I answer, concerning this question, that this request cannot be sought except after many preliminaries, and when these preliminaries are fulfilled, love of God, blessed be He, is born from them; but whoever aims directly at it cannot attain it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:2: The preliminaries he should establish beforehand within his soul are: two unifications of the heart, two submissions, two reckonings, and two examinations. The two unifications of the heart: one of them to unify the heart in the unity of the Creator, and the second to unify one's deeds for His sake and to serve Him for His honor alone. The two submissions: one, submission to God, blessed be He, and the second, submission to those who fear God and His chosen ones. The two reckonings: one, his reckoning with his soul concerning what he owes to God for His constant goodness, and the second, his reckoning with his soul concerning His concealing his sins and being patient with him and forgiving him. The two examinations: one, the examination of what happened to the earlier generations, by studying the books of the prophets and the words of the ancients, as it is written (Psalms 143:5) "I remember the days of old"; and the second, the examination of the world, in what he sees of the wonders of the Creator, blessed be He, in His creatures. I have already explained in this book general principles on this matter, as much as I am able, sufficient for one who understands and aims at what will bring his salvation and deliverance in this world and the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:3: When he sets all this in order and joins to it abstinence from the pleasures of this world and its desires, and understands the Creator's greatness, His essence, and His truth, and grasps the smallness of his own soul's worth, its meagerness and lowliness, and afterward recognizes the Creator's abundant goodness toward him and the greatness of His kindness with him - then love of God will be found in the believer, close upon this, with a complete heart, the true purity of his soul, and his yearning for Him with effort, diligence, and alacrity, similar to what is said (Isaiah 26:9) "my soul desires You in the night," and it says (Psalms 42:3) "my soul thirsts for God" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:4: Concerning the matter of examination, I have also chosen to quote his words in the Gate of Examination, chapter 1, speaking of the general matters comprising all the particulars of examination - his words, in chapter 4, in explaining several signs of wisdom in creatures that we can discern: the categories of wisdom established in creatures, for most of their kinds and individuals, are seven. One of them is the sign of wisdom seen in the roots and foundations of the world, in seeing the earth standing in the middle, and the water adjacent, above it, and the air adjacent to them, and the fire above, according to a scale and measure from which nothing changes, each one steadfast in its own place, particular to it and bounded for it; and the sea stands, and the waters are bound within it, not passing beyond its boundary, even if its waves roar and its winds storm, as it is written (Job 38:10-11) "and I broke for it My decree, and set a bar and doors," and it says, "thus far you shall come and no further." And it says concerning the standing of heaven and earth (Psalms 119:89-90) "forever, O Lord, Your word stands firm in the heavens; Your faithfulness is to all generations" - as David the king, peace be upon him, composed concerning this matter in the psalm (Psalms 104:1) "bless the Lord, O my soul."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:5: The second category: the sign of wisdom seen in the human species, which is the small world, etc., and to this David the king, peace be upon him, alluded, saying (Psalms 8:2) "O Lord, our Master, how mighty is Your Name in all the earth."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:6: And the third, the sign of wisdom seen in the composition of man and the joining of his body and the powers of his soul and the light of the intellect that the Creator singled out in him, giving him thereby superiority over the rest of the non-speaking creatures, and he is comparable to the great world and likened to it in his roots and foundations; to this Job alluded, saying (Job 10:10-12) "did You not pour me out like milk," etc., "You have clothed me with skin and flesh," etc., "You have granted me life and kindness," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:7: And the fourth, the sign of wisdom seen in the other species of living things, from small to great, among them those that fly, those that swim, those that crawl, and those that walk on four legs, according to the differences of their forms and attributes and their use and benefit and rank in the world, as is mentioned in the passage where the Creator rebuked Job in order to awaken him (Job 38:41) "who provides for the raven its prey," and the rest of what is told there of the kinds of beasts of the wild and of the water.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:8: And the fifth, the sign of wisdom seen in plants and minerals prepared for man's benefit, and the ways he benefits from them according to the differences of their natures, their compositions, and their powers - and the ancients have already mentioned this matter in their books according to their grasp, as it is written (I Kings 5:13) "and he spoke of the trees," etc., "from the cedar that is in Lebanon even to the hyssop that grows in the wall," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:9: And the sixth, the sign of wisdom seen in the sciences and crafts and works that the Creator, blessed be He, prepared for man to complete his welfare, and the causes of his allotted sustenance and his other general and specific benefits; to this he alluded in saying (Job 38:36) "who has put wisdom in the innermost parts, or given understanding to the mind?" and he says (Proverbs 2:6) "for the Lord gives wisdom, from His mouth come knowledge and understanding."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:10: And the seventh, the sign of wisdom seen in the establishment of the Torah and statutes by which to serve the Creator, blessed be He, through which one who is diligent in them attains benefits of this world immediately and the reward of the World to Come in the end, as Scripture says (Isaiah 55:2) "listen diligently to Me and eat what is good, and let your soul delight itself in abundance," and it says, "incline your ear and come to Me, listen, that your soul may live." And dependent on this are the matters of leaders, through whom the order of governance of the other nations and their benefit is arranged, and they stand for them in the place of Torah in worldly matters alone; and it has already been said that the level of nature compared to the Torah is like the level of the servant compared to his master, for the powers of nature govern the world according to what is fitting for the Torah, as it is written (Exodus 23:25) "and you shall serve the Lord your God, and He will bless your bread and your water," and it says (ibid. 15:26) "and He said, if you diligently heed the voice of the Lord your God, and do what is right in His eyes," etc., and many like these - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:11: Know that although it is true, what the pious master, author of Chovot HaLevavot, writes, that examination of worldly matters is what arouses love, and for this reason we were compelled to quote his words on matters of examination, likewise, along the secret way, examination of worldly matters arouses love; therefore we must elaborate on matters of examination in order to arouse love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:12: The reason is that the world endures only through Chesed, as Scripture says (Psalms 89:3) "I have said, the world shall be built with kindness" - it is not written "is built" but "shall be built," for the world is built anew every single day through Chesed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:13: This matter is likewise explained in the Zohar, portion of Tzav (30b), on the verse (Psalms 7:12) "and God is angry every day" - his words: "'God' [El] - in every place, the abundant illumination of the supernal wisdom, and it stands in its existence; and were it not that this 'El' is aroused in the world, the world could not stand even one hour before the harsh judgments aroused in the world every day - this is [the meaning of] (Genesis 2:4) 'these are the generations of the heavens and the earth when they were created [behibaram]' - do not read 'behibaram' but 'be'Avraham' [through Abraham] - they stand through the arousal of Abraham. And when Abraham is aroused in the world, all those judgments found every single day are pushed outside and do not stand before him - this is [the meaning of] 'and God is angry every day' - it is not written 'is angered' or 'angered every day' but 'is angry every day' - every single day judgment is found, and He pushes it outside, and He stands and sweetens the world - this is [the meaning of] (Psalms 42:9) 'by day the Lord commands His kindness' - and were it not for this, the world could not stand even one moment, and therefore everything stands for Abraham's sake" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:14: With this passage we understand what we say in the Yotzer prayer, "and in His goodness He renews every single day continually the act of Creation" - and likewise "who renews in His goodness every day continually" - for "good" [tov] is the secret of the known Chesed, and the light of Chesed flowing every day to renew all existing things in the world and give them permanence is the renewal, similar to the moon renewed by the light of the sun - this is what we say, "as it is said, to Him who makes great lights," etc. - and the meaning is that the verse informs us of the matter of renewal by saying "to Him who makes," meaning that He is always making great lights, for the reason that "His kindness is eternal," since Chesed is what renews them and makes them every day, and for this reason Scripture does not say that He "made" great lights, which would imply the past, at the time of the world's creation, but rather "who makes," that every single day He makes and renews. This is likewise "who makes new things," said in the blessing of Yotzer, in "God, blessed," and this corresponds to Chesed, as we find it said (Isaiah 52:3) "the kindness of God, all the day."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:15: It may be that in order for us to remember the matter that His goodness is renewed every day, which indicates that He, blessed be He, created the world out of nothing and renews it every day, our Sages, of blessed memory, instituted the matters of the blessings in the Name and Kingship: YHVH - since He brings beings into existence; and "King" - that He watches over them, like a king who watches over and has compassion on his servants - so the Holy One, blessed be He, watches over the world since He created it, to give it permanence and endurance forever, so that His flow never ceases from the world for a moment, and the light is always renewed corresponding to the [reciting] believers. And we say "who creates the fruit," etc. - the intent is likewise along this way, that were it not for His flow flowing to sustain existing things, that fruit or that matter would not have been created; for were it not for the water and dews falling every day, there would be no sustaining the world, and likewise the sun's shining to sweeten the fruits of the tree, as it says (Deuteronomy 33:14) "and with the precious fruits brought forth by the sun, and with the precious things put forth by the moons" - for there are fruits in the world ripened by the sun and some by the moon, and were the Holy One, blessed be He, not to make the sun and moon shine every day, the world could not endure. If so, through them the act of Creation is renewed, and every day the Holy One, blessed be He, creates the world anew, and to this our Sages, of blessed memory, instituted, in the blessing of Yotzer, "who renews in His goodness every day continually," etc., and likewise the matter of "Yotzer HaMe'orot" [Creator of the Lights], for through them is the renewal of the world and the act of Creation, and the whole of the renewal is from the side of Chesed, which renews it, as we have explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:16: In the Tikkunim (145a), it says that the sun at first goes forth red, and afterward whitens - his words: "and because it draws from Gevurah at first, the sun goes forth red; afterward it is clothed in Chesed, which is white, and in it the sun's wrath is stilled" - so far. This aspect too is among the observations the discerning reader must make regarding the creation of the world, as we shall explain.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:17: Also the reality of the creation of several things in the world that are the endurance of the whole world is through Chesed, and several things David the king, peace be upon him, mentions in the Great Hallel psalm, concerning the flowing of springs, living waters day and night without ceasing - the waters flow from the side of Chesed, and through the endurance of the world, Chesed flows without interruption and descends below. And the fire is in between, since it is judgment, ascending above everything, since a small amount suffices; and the air is in between, and everything is made and arranged in the order of His supernal attributes, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:18: Likewise, what is explained in the Zohar, portion of Vaera (24a), that the south is dry and arid from heat, while the north is moist with water - and it would seem fitting for it to be the reverse, since "from the north evil breaks forth," and it would seem fitting for the fire and heat to be there. And they resolve that the Holy One, blessed be He, made them to blend, and we shall quote some of his words below. And the fire, from this aspect, is mercy, for when the waters freeze on the side of the north, they are released and flow from the side of the south because of this fire - and with this the wording of Rashbi is understood (Zohar, Bereishit 29b); and likewise, in the time of cold, fire is mercy and kindness.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:19: Along these lines is the matter of the shining of the sun and the blowing of the winds, as is explained in the midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 28:11): Rabbi Levi and the Rabbis - Rabbi Levi says, all that creatures raise through commandments and good deeds in this world, it suffices that the Holy One, blessed be He, shines the sun for them, as it is said (Ecclesiastes 1:5) "and the sun rises and the sun sets." And the Rabbis say, all that the righteous raise through commandments and good deeds in this world, it suffices that the Holy One, blessed be He, renews their faces like the disc of the sun, as it is said (Judges 5:31) "and those who love Him are like the sun going forth in its might." Rabbi Yannai said: as the way of the world, a person takes one measure of meat from the market - how much labor he labors, how much pain he suffers, until he cooks it! Yet creatures sleep on their beds, and the Holy One, blessed be He, brings back winds and raises clouds and grows plants and sweetens the fruits, and they give only the reward of the Omer for it - this is [the meaning of] (Leviticus 23:10) "and you shall bring the Omer of the firstfruits of your harvest to the priest" - so far. And they elaborate further there on the merit of the wind to dry the earth in the rainy season and to winnow the straw so that the wheat be clean, see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:20: Here, all these things and the like are all from the side of Chesed, and therefore it says in the passage I quoted that the Holy One, blessed be He, grows plants, etc., and they give only the Omer to the priest - and it is known that the priest is Chesed - "Your Thummim and Urim are with Your pious one" (Deuteronomy 33:8) - and the meaning is that since everything comes from Chesed, the firstfruits should be brought near to Chesed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:21: Likewise, several things David the king, peace be upon him, mentions in the Great Hallel psalm, which has twenty-six [verses of] "for His kindness is eternal" - (Psalms 136:5) "to Him who made the heavens with understanding, for His kindness is eternal," etc., "to Him who spread the earth upon the waters, for His kindness is eternal," "the sun to rule by day, for His kindness is eternal," "the moon and stars," etc., and several other miracles mentioned in the psalm, all through Chesed - "to Him who struck Egypt," etc., "to Him who divided the Red Sea into parts," etc., "to Him who led His people through the wilderness," etc. Were we to elaborate on the explanation of each and every one of these, we would stray from the purpose of our discourse; our intent is only to arouse the discourse, so that a person may consider and discern His kindness, blessed be He, performing so many acts with us, and thereby cleave to the side of His kindness, becoming a lover - for the lover cleaves to the side of Chesed, as is explained in chapter 2, as it is written (Isaiah 41:8) "the seed of Abraham My beloved," and it is said (Psalms 31:24) "love the Lord, all His pious ones," and the like.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:22: Therefore, we must explain, from the matter of examination, three general principles, comprising all the particulars of examination explained in Chovot HaLevavot: the first, the examination of the world and its particulars - the living beings, cattle, birds, and plants, and, among the upper beings, the firmaments, sun and moon, etc. The second, the examination of the creation of man in general and his governance from the day of his birth to the day of his death. The third, the examination of the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, for Israel and the miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performs with them in general. And when a person discerns His kindnesses, blessed be He, in the particulars to be explained, he will recognize and know that He is one, alone, and there is none else, that He brings them into being and He sustains them - this is that "ahavah" [love] sums to "echad" [one, numerically] - and when he knows that He is one, he will cleave to Him in love properly. This is why, in the third passage of the tefillin, which is Shema Yisrael, which is explained in the portion of Va'etchanan (Zohar 267a) to correspond to Chesed, unity is mentioned in it, "the Lord our God, the Lord is one," and afterward the matter of love is mentioned, "and you shall love the Lord your God," etc. - for the essential service, of giving over one's soul in love of one's Maker, cannot be firmly established toward Him except after knowing that He is one alone, who created him for His glory, etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:23: These two actions particular to Chesed that I have explained - one, the endurance and renewal of the world through it, and the second, the matter of unity - Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in the Pekudin, in the commandment of tefillin - his words (Zohar, end of Bo 43b): "the third passage, Shema - this is the secret of the right, called supernal Chesed, which unifies the unity of everything into the four directions, and the Holy One, blessed be He, arranges through it the arrangement of the whole world, and this is what spreads in every direction, even within the lowest depths" - so far, as relevant to us.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:24: The examination of the world in general - one should fittingly consider that this world was created with the thirty-two "gods" [elohim] mentioned in the account of Creation, which are thirty-two paths; and we learn at the beginning of Sefer Yetzirah (chapter 1, mishnah 1), "with thirty-two wondrous paths of wisdom, YH YHVH Tzeva'ot engraved His universe." Although this Mishnah has several interpretations, for our purpose the plain sense suffices: that through the thirty-two paths of wisdom came the creation of all things existing in the world. This is what Scripture says (Psalms 104:24) "how many are Your works, O Lord; You have made them all with wisdom," etc. - we find that the power of His wisdom, blessed be He, spread through all existing things to give them permanence, and every single herb and beast and animal has an angel and a supernal spiritual power, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (Bereishit Rabbah 10:6): "do you know the ordinances of the heavens? Can you set their dominion over the earth?" (Job 38:33) - there is not a single herb below that does not have a constellation in the firmament that strikes it and says to it, "grow!" And this is the reason for [the prohibition of] mixed species [kilayim], as is explained in the Zohar, portion of Kedoshim (86b). Rabbi Yosef Gikatilla, peace be upon him, writes that concerning this it is said (Genesis 1:11) "let the earth put forth grass, herb yielding seed after its kind" - "after its kind," literally, according to that power coming to it from above, from the kind particular to it. So too it is said concerning birds and fish (Genesis 1:21) "which the waters brought forth abundantly, after their kinds" - "after their kinds," literally, according to the flow of that kind bestowed upon it from the heavens.
